infosec.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
infosec.summary: A 16-year-old buffer overflow in TianoCore EDK2's PXE Base Code driver (CVE-2026-97631, CVSS 9.5), the reference UEFI code behind most server firmware, allowed an attacker to send an oversized ICMP error during network boot and execute ring 0 code before Secure Boot and the TPM chain of trust loaded. An AMI pull request leaked the fix months ahead of a January coordinated disclosure, although exploitation required local network access and per-model address tuning. Defenders should request patched firmware from their UEFI vendors, disable PXE boot where feasible, and monitor network boot segments for anomalous ICMP traffic.

infosec.title: Hackers Target US Election Commission, Forcing Online System Shutdown Days Before Midterms

infosec.title: What are Security Logs?
infosec.summary: Logs are structured records of security events in formats such as JSON, CSV, Syslog, and Windows Event Logs. Security engineers need to apply transformations to event logs to normalize the various formats and fields, making the data uniform for correlation and composite detections.

infosec.title: Not Only ARTEX: The Different Levels AI is Used in Attacks Targeting Japan
infosec.summary: TrendAI examined three attacker infrastructures targeting Japan, documenting autonomous attacks, AI-assisted planning, and suspected AI-written tools. CyberStrikeAI coordinated 44 agents against at least 19 organizations. Another operator scanned 6,000 Japanese IPs and stole hundreds of thousands of records through default credentials. A third used recovered VPN credentials to enter corporate networks. Evidence came from exposed attacker files. Victim-side confirmation remains incomplete.

infosec.title: How Anchorage Digital and Turnkey verify code with AWS Nitro Enclaves
infosec.summary: Anchorage Digital and Turnkey ran the open-source VisualSign transaction parser inside AWS Nitro Enclaves, where each parsed result was signed with an ephemeral P-256 key and bundled with a Nitro attestation document whose PCRs wallets checked against reproducible builds. The design let wallets prove that unmodified, audited code decoded a transaction, removing blind trust in crypto transaction signing by providing verifiable attestation rather than relying solely on network identity or operator trust. The open-source awsnitroverifier Go library handles certificate-chain and PCR validation, which any organization can use to verify their services running in AWS Nitro.

Two thefts involved ramming security escorts' vehicles. One $10 million shipment disappeared after its tracking coordinates were apparently spoofed.

Completing attacker-initiated authorization gives attackers Microsoft 365 tokens. ANY.RUN identified obfuscated JavaScript and a PHP backend tracking victim sessions, IP addresses, and geolocation, and the backend repeatedly polls for authentication completion.

data.title: Best Practices for Single Row Lookups (Point Queries)
data.summary: DataFusion can perform surprisingly well on point lookups when tuned for retrieval instead of analytics. The biggest gains came from storage layout and execution choices that minimize unnecessary work, such as sorted Parquet files, right-sized row groups, metadata caching, and prepared statements. The broader lesson is that analytical engines can serve low-latency reads if the workload is designed deliberately.

data.title: How JD.com Built a Lakestream with Apache Fluss and Apache Hudi
data.summary: JD replaced parallel streaming and batch training-data pipelines with a staged migration: write once to Fluss, tier to Hudi, and union fresh plus historical reads. The difficult part is consistency: workers coordinate a single Hudi commit per tiering round and report matched stream offsets only after it completes. That pattern enables rollback-safe catch-up, but leaves schema evolution and dynamic bucketing unresolved.

data.title: The paper that split the database in four: inside Azure SQL Database Hyperscale, aka Socrates
data.summary: Azure SQL once kept four full copies of each database, which capped practical size at around 4 TB. The 2019 Socrates paper separated the log from storage, so durability and availability could scale apart. This change in approach let Hyperscale reach 100 TB, halve storage copies, and restore a 50 TB database in minutes.

data.title: The 2026 Cloud Data Warehouse Benchmark

Databricks had the smallest latency increase from 1 GB to 1 TB (3.7x versus MotherDuck's 30x), with tuning and autoscaling disabled throughout.

data.summary: AI code generation is helping database engines game ClickBench. data.summary: Netflix made failure diagnosis more reliable by using LLMs to identify the exact log spans behind an error and provide on-demand root-cause analysis, instead of asking models to digest entire logs. Favorites, Screenshots, and Trash are pinned by default, while albums, people and pets, places, and other categories get carousels that can be hidden or reordered. The update arrives with Google Photos version 7.97 through a server-side switch, with no broader release date announced.

design.title: Designing for People with ADHD
design.summary: ADHD affects about 5% of people and stems from differences in how the brain develops focus, planning, and self-regulation. It is not a matter of willpower. Helpful patterns include reminders for unfinished drafts, chunked long forms, gradual disclosure of options, and visible progress, while autoplay and infinite scroll are best avoided. ADHD often overlaps with autism, dyslexia, and anxiety, so designing for it tends to help several groups at once.

design.title: One size doesn't fit all: rethinking “good design” across cultures
design.summary: Ideas such as clarity, simplicity, restraint, and functionality are often treated as universal measures of good design even though they emerged from particular Western histories and cultural contexts. Design traditions excluded from the dominant canon can use decoration, complexity, symbolism, and craft in ways that are deeply functional within their cultures, challenging assumptions that minimalism is inherently more sophisticated or understandable. Evaluating design more broadly requires asking who established prevailing standards of taste, whose histories were documented and taught, and whether a design successfully serves its specific cultural purpose rather than conforming to a supposedly universal aesthetic.

design.title: A select should tell you something
design.summary: Customizable HTML selects can now include previews, secondary information, warnings, and other context that helps people recognize the right option instead of deciphering text labels. Practical examples include showing fonts in their actual typefaces, displaying current local times instead of UTC offsets, aligning delivery prices for comparison, and distinguishing people with identical names by job title and department. The technique progressively enhances the native `select`, so unsupported browsers can retain familiar controls while richer desktop experiences provide more useful information without replacing built-in semantics and keyboard behavior.

design.title: Animated Architecture Diagrams from Plain Text
design.summary: Declare semantic nodes, flows, and timed beats in reviewable text. Markdy compiles browser-native motion graphics that stay version-controlled, PR-friendly, and AI-native.

design.title: Open-Source CAD for AI Agents
design.summary: The text-to-cad plugin gives your agent local workflows for generating 3D models as STEP, GLB, STL, or 3MF files. It also does design for manufacturing checks, generates engineering drawings, and connects to popular 3D printing, sheet metal, and CNC fabrication services.

design.title: Make Wild Visual Effects in Your Browser
design.summary: Ladybug is an effects studio for pictures, video, type, and sound.

design.title: How Mother Design turned a séance into a new identity for Purple Garden
design.summary: Mother Design began Purple Garden's rebrand with a séance, chakra reading, and automatic drawing workshop, using the resulting forms and feelings to build an identity around spirituality as “A Living Practice.” A whimsical wordmark, crystal-like guidance glyph, warm purple palette, tactile imagery, living typography inspired by cymatic patterns, and expressive motion create an immersive system without relying on familiar psychic-industry clichés. The process moved between physical experimentation, traditional design software, and AI tools, deliberately introducing unpredictability into both the creative process and the finished identity.

design.title: The Software Factory Forgot About Design
design.summary: A four-station workflow of Linear, Paper, a coding agent, and review brings design into the software factory, where issues otherwise turn straight into pull requests. Linear holds the intent, Paper hosts agent-drafted HTML and CSS designs made before implementation, and the coding agent builds from both issue and design. Review checks the build against intent, but agents still lack the history behind decisions, such as past designs, analytics, and design-system reasoning.

design.title: The New York Times turns 175 with an identity, events and a campaign
design.summary: The New York Times is marking its 175th anniversary with a visual identity, campaign, and program of events that use the publication's history as material rather than simply commemorating its age. Familiar elements from its editorial and typographic heritage are reframed across contemporary applications, connecting decades of journalism with the publication's current cultural role. The system demonstrates how an established institution can celebrate recognizable brand equity while giving historical assets new relevance instead of replacing them.

design.title: This Creative Agency's Website is Giving Me Tumblr 2000s Vibes, and I'm Here for It
design.summary: Denver's Bound Agency has a handmade, scrapbook-style site by Wunder Werkz that evokes 2000s Tumblr, with a handwritten logo, doodled icons, and tarot cards.

design.title: struggle together
design.summary: AI can remove much of the difficulty involved in learning and making things, but some of that struggle builds judgment, understanding, relationships, and the ability to create things with other people that none could have made alone.

design.title: Stefan Sagmeister's Artworks Turn Global Data into Good News at La Gaîté Lyrique
design.summary: Stefan Sagmeister's solo show "Finally, Something Good" at La Gaîté Lyrique turns UN and World Bank data into artworks arguing that health, democracy, and equality have improved.

marketing.title: Make launch videos, demos and ads in minutes using Clueso
marketing.summary: Every launch, campaign and feature release needs video. Making one still takes several days, an editor, and costly back-and-forth over revisions. Clueso cuts that to minutes. Hand it a screen recording, deck, doc or idea, and its AI agent turns it into a polished, on-brand video with your footage, AI voiceover, motion graphics and b-roll. 🎥 Start from inspiration: share a video you love, and Clueso adapts it to your vision. 🎨 Stay on brand: your logo, fonts and colors on every video. 🔎 Stay in control: edit any scene by hand, or ask the agent. Join 50,000+ people making stunning videos with Clueso. Start creating for free →

marketing.title: Chatbots Put PR Back On The Brand Agenda. Social Listening Decides What It Should Say
marketing.summary: AI search is giving PR a larger role in marketing because chatbots use third-party coverage to answer questions and recommend brands. One forecast projects that PR and earned media budgets will double by 2027 as more consumers use AI chatbots instead of traditional search. Social listening also gives brands real-time audience research, helping teams identify which creative ideas resonate and which risk backlash before investing further. As AI makes content cheaper to produce, audience understanding and independent brand credibility become more valuable.

marketing.title: Ozempic is changing how Americans spend money, and the numbers are startling
marketing.summary: GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are reshaping consumer spending across food, fitness, and retail. 11% of American adults use these medications, with 26% of users spending more on clothing and 36% more on jewelry. Meanwhile, household spending at fast-food restaurants drops nearly 9% after 6-8 months on the drugs. Users are also buying fewer sweets and sugary drinks while spending more on fresh produce and protein.

marketing.title: Spotting CTR decay early: how to catch ad creative fatigue
marketing.summary: Creative fatigue shows up as one ad's CTR sliding week after week below its own launch-week level while frequency climbs and the other ads in the same ad set hold steady. A single early drop that then flattens is normal settling, not fatigue. CPM rising on every ad at once points to the auction or the calendar instead, and frequency rising while reach plateaus points to an exhausted audience. Meta's own “Creative fatigue” status only appears once cost per result doubles, well after spend is lost.

marketing.title: I Analyzed the Lead Magnet Funnel of a 190,000 LinkedIn Creator
marketing.summary: An audit of a creator's lead magnet funnel reveals ways to turn email subscribers into clients. Keep landing pages focused with a clear promise and visible signup form. Use the thank-you page to book calls or collect information for personalized follow-ups instead of showing a generic confirmation. In the welcome email, build credibility with personal stories and testimonials while previewing upcoming lessons. Encourage replies to improve deliverability and let eager subscribers access the full course immediately.

marketing.title: Still think of Wix as a DIY website builder? There's a side you're missing...
marketing.summary: For organizations that manage 100s or 1,000s of websites - dealer networks, franchises, partners, local chapters - the challenge isn't building websites. It's giving local teams the freedom to manage them while maintaining centralized brand standards, security and control. Learn how Wix keeps thousands of external websites on-brand on the Wix Enterprise blog.

marketing.title: The evolution of web series on YouTube: Microdramas
marketing.summary: Creators are turning Shorts into serialized dramas with short episodes and audience-driven storylines. YouTube is adding tools to organize episodes into series and improve discovery. New monetization options will also let creators offer members-only episodes. Brands can partner with creators to integrate products into these short-form stories.

marketing.title: How to win BFCM (Webinar)
marketing.summary: Verbose's Lifecycle Live workshop brings together lifecycle marketing experts to share BFCM campaign strategies. Joined by Hightouch's Luke Kline, the session covers contingency planning and cross-channel messaging. Attendees will learn how to drive customer engagement and long-term value beyond discounts.

marketing.title: Third-party citation optimization prioritization in an AI search era: A framework with worksheet & Claude skill
marketing.summary: This guide shares a framework for prioritizing third-party websites that influence AI search recommendations. It scores opportunities across 6 criteria, including citation influence, brand association, and business value. The guide includes a worksheet and a Claude skill to identify valuable targets such as independent reviews and comparison guides.

marketing.title: How we built and launched a viral research campaign in partnership with LinkedIn
marketing.summary: Partnering with a brand that has complementary data and a shared interest can make original research stand out in a crowded market and expand its reach. Semrush combined its AI citation data with LinkedIn's content and engagement data to analyze around 89,000 LinkedIn URLs cited by AI search tools. The study found that 95% of cited posts were original content rather than reshares, and most cited posts averaged just 15 to 25 reactions. Semrush and LinkedIn coordinated media outreach, employee advocacy, social promotion, and launch timing to reach both audiences and generate strong media coverage, tens of thousands of visits, and dozens of signups. The collaboration also created new opportunities for guest content and speaking engagements beyond the initial campaign.

marketing.title: The Anatomy of the Best-Performing Onboarding Paywalls
marketing.summary: Multi-page onboarding paywalls convert 47% better than single-page ones, and conversion peaks at 3 screens. The top performers follow the same sequence, a free-trial promise with no prices, then a trial-end reminder, then the offer. The reminder screen is the strongest single signal, lifting conversion from 8.7% to 14.8% by removing the fear of forgetting to cancel. Leading with one yearly plan beats the common yearly-plus-monthly picker by about 1.5x, and an abandon offer for users who cancel checkout adds roughly 18% revenue per view.

marketing.title: GEO Doesn't Create Demand. It Captures Demand That Already Exists.
marketing.summary: AI answers also only reach buyers already in-market, yet GEO is often judged like a performance channel.

marketing.title: TikTok expands into restaurant guides with ‘Must Eat' feature
marketing.summary: The guide pulls recommendations from more than 40 million posts and comments into city lists filterable by cuisine, price, and location, with OpenTable booking for select restaurants.

marketing.title: 6 cool things we built into the new vector.co
marketing.summary: Vector revamped its brand and website for its ABM launch, adding interactive features and a Claude design system for on-brand content creation.

founders.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR
founders.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach founders, operators and startup leaders where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities .

founders.title: The future of the firm
founders.summary: Managing people used to be something you earned after years of grunt work. In this post, two people at OpenAI who were running teams of agents at 24 walk through where AI could end up on a company's org chart. In the simplest version, nobody changes seats, so everyone just becomes a manager (an accountant still owns the accounting while agents do the spreadsheet work). The accounting team doesn't shrink either, because the rest of the company is getting more productive and needs more accounting than before.

founders.title: Databricks & the future of the firm
founders.summary: Most companies don't need smarter AI models to unlock major productivity gains. The bigger bottleneck is context: models lack access to internal knowledge, unwritten processes, and the judgment sitting in employees' heads. Databricks is building a shared system of record that gives agents this context, alongside permissions and feedback on their work. This could reduce management layers devoted to moving information around, while shifting employees toward defining tasks, delegating execution, and judging results. The lasting competitive advantage would come from capturing what a company learns, so its AI systems improve even when it switches models.

founders.title: What Comes After Selling Work?
founders.summary: Companies spend about $6 on services for every $1 on software, so a lot of AI startups now want to be the law firm instead of selling it software. Selling the work itself might only be step one. Big firms are building their own AI (Kirkland & Ellis is putting $500M into its stack), so give the service away and make money on the deals and data that run through it. For example, Rockwell runs a free benefits concierge for employees at mid-market companies, so it sits right in front of their healthcare spending.

founders.title: Design the Dinner for the Follow-Up
founders.summary: Most customer dinners are planned around the night itself, and the "great meeting you" email afterward gets ignored. One conference dinner turned into $4M in revenue for Recall.ai. The trick was to put a rep at every table whose only job was seating customers next to prospects, so prospects heard about the product from people who already trusted it. Reps then sent each prospect an intro to the customer they sat beside ("You two were talking about X at the dinner"). That email is much harder to ignore than a thank-you note.

founders.title: Smart reports, surveys, and pooled group budgets for Claude Enterprise
founders.summary: Claude Smart reports surface what a team gets done with Claude and what that work costs. Admins can now create surveys to get feedback on how the team is working with AI. Anthropic has introduced Pool group budgets, giving teams a shared monthly budget. Member limits are still available as a guardrail against unusually high individual use.

founders.title: Introducing the Slack Code API: Your agents, your team, one code channel
founders.summary: The Slack Code API allows agents to start code channels, add relevant people and files, post updates as they work, and archive channels when the work is done. It enables teams to work together with agents on tasks with the same shared context. Users can see exactly what agents are doing and who approved it, and workspace controls and data boundaries are built in. Users can choose what agents and models they want to use to suit their needs.

founders.title: AI traffic insights now available in Vercel Observability
founders.summary: Vercel now shows how AI bots use your site, including which pages assistants fetch when someone asks them a question and which pages return errors to those bots. Querying the numbers from the CLI requires Observability Plus.

founders.title: How I Built the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World
founders.summary: Spawn is a company with 10 people that spends 30 times its payroll on AI tokens. The company ships almost as much as Anthropic, with 77,000 substantial changes in the last 30 days. Its work is done by a fleet of permanent AI agents that each own a part of the company. Each new model improvement has made the team faster and more coherent, and pointed the company's velocity more in the right direction.

founders.title: The 90% gross margin era is over
founders.summary: AI companies need a new way to pitch their economics. The cost of serving customers is much higher with AI. Companies need to separate gross margin by customer and gross margin by pricing cohort. When changing pricing, you ideally want to show investors that customers on the new model have higher margins than those on the old one, and that the gap keeps widening.

founders.title: Roll-Up Targets Shouldn't Just Be Cheap
founders.summary: One acquisition target was turning away work worth 4–5 times last year's revenue because it couldn't afford more staff.

founders.title: How to steal your competitor's customers for <$100
founders.summary: Wispr Flow pays affiliates $35 to bring over paying Granola users, while Granola pays $20 to recruit new ones.

founders.title: Which business advantages can a solo developer build?
founders.summary: Review what work a proposed moat would require every week, and then decide whether customers value the result enough to support that work.

founders.title: System of Action
founders.summary: System of Action is a series of essays that details what it takes for vertical software to win in the age of AI.

founders.title: Developers ask AI which tool to use. Here's how Webflow tracked the answer
founders.summary: Being named is easy, but being described correctly requires a bit of effort.

crypto.title: Moody's assigns investment-grade ratings to Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin
crypto.summary: Moody's gave RLUSD an A2 long-term and P-1 short-term deposit rating. It cited reserve credit quality and market value, coverage, liquidity, redemption arrangements, segregation, and third-party custody. The reserve is mostly short-term US government assets and cash held at BNY (Aa1), and the custodian targets 103% coverage. Ripple says it is the first stablecoin to get an investment-grade rating from Moody's. RLUSD has a $2.5B market cap and is used mainly inside Ripple's payments and as collateral in Ripple Prime. The ratings could fall if reserve quality, coverage, or liquidity weakens. Ripple also just got final OCC approval for Ripple National Trust Bank.

crypto.title: Bithumb hacked through employee system
crypto.summary: Bithumb, South Korea's second-largest exchange, said an outsider breached the internal mobile system employees use for work and messaging, and personal information was stolen. No crypto funds were reported lost. It says the system is separate from its trading platform, so customer assets can't be reached that way. It has not said how many people's data were exposed or whether deposits or withdrawals were affected. Regulators are also assessing Daishin Securities, which said data for 38,490 customers leaked, and Mirae Asset Global Investments, which blocked abnormal access. The regulator's governor said cyberattacks had hit 16 financial firms as of October 14. In February, Bithumb mistakenly credited customers with 620,000 BTC instead of 620,000 won.

crypto.title: Link Balance: How Stripe Built the Infrastructure for Agentic Commerce
crypto.summary: Stripe Link balance is a pre-funded wallet for AI agents that removes per-transaction approval by letting consumers deposit funds and set spending limits upfront, with Instinct as the first integrated assistant. The stack routes fiat through Stripe Crypto Onramp into dollar-denominated stablecoins on Tempo, uses Privy's non-custodial wallets for key management and signing, then converts back to virtual debit cards via Stripe Issuing, so merchants receive standard card transactions with no crypto integration required. Agentic purchases through Link grew 38x in one month, with Muse reporting over 25% of weekly users shopping via agent. The architecture deploys stablecoins as settlement infrastructure rather than a user-facing asset class, keeping crypto rails invisible to both merchants and consumers while solving the approval-friction bottleneck that has constrained autonomous agent commerce.

crypto.title: Fynd AMM: The First AMM that Outbids Competition in Real-Time
crypto.summary: Fynd AMM introduces a last-mover pricing mechanism where the pool sets its price during routing after observing all competing quotes, rather than submitting a fixed price before DEX aggregators query it. Traditional AMMs and propAMMs bid blind, causing LPs to either overbid on trades they win or lose trades they could have priced to win. A backtest of 60 ETH/USDG trades on Robinhood shows a standard 30 bps pool captures half the trades but collects only 37% of available fees, while Fynd AMM charges the maximum fee that still wins each trade, generating 2.7x more LP revenue. The protocol is launching on Ekubo's concentrated liquidity infrastructure and is already integrated on Robinhood and Base.

crypto.title: The Long Road to Bitcoin Payments
crypto.summary: Spiral, Block's Bitcoin-focused subsidiary, published a report arguing Bitcoin payments infrastructure is production-ready but adoption remains a demand problem, not a technology gap. Lightning runs in production, self-custodial wallets have abstracted most complexity, and over one million US merchants can accept Bitcoin through Square. The strategic concern is that major payment providers are now updating financial rails with stablecoin support, and if those rails exclude Bitcoin natively, switching costs could lock the current payments upgrade cycle into stablecoin infrastructure. Spiral is issuing a call for moonshot ideas to accelerate Bitcoin payment adoption before that window closes.

crypto.title: The Internet Is No Longer for Humans
crypto.summary: CVE publications hit 14,939 in September alone, four times the 2025 monthly average, with Critical and High severity vulnerabilities up 161% year-over-year and now comprising more than half of all new records. The surge coincides with a structural shift: internet security was architected around human attackers, so CAPTCHAs, rate limits, and fraud detection all break when AI agents can solve challenges in milliseconds and fire thousands of requests per second. Proposed fixes are crypto-native: verifiable on-chain agent identity, cryptographic authorization proofs, and machine-to-machine payment rails like x402. Hacktron is positioned as a security scanner for this agent-centric web, using the same AI techniques attackers deploy.

crypto.title: Buybacks do work
crypto.summary: Buybacks mechanically raise price, and crypto needs them because token holders have no legal rights. There is positive evidence for buybacks. However, buybacks compound slowly and fail if the business is a flash in the pan. Teams that ran points programs have a moral duty to show alignment through buybacks. Investors should buy coins where the protocol is the marginal buyer.

crypto.title: Why Pump.fun isn't the real problem
crypto.summary: The “Pump.fun is the enemy” backlash repeats what happened to OpenSea when NFTs faded. When a speculative asset class stops paying, the platform tied to it becomes the villain. Memecoins are exhausted, liquidity is fragmented, and average traders now compete against professionals. Removing Pump.fun wouldn't fix that, because another platform would take its place. People are seeking a platform-level fix for a market-level problem. However, some of Pump.fun's decisions deserve criticism regardless.

crypto.title: Aero hits 10.5% of all DEX spot volume this week
crypto.summary: Aero is processing 10.5% of all DEX spot volume so far this week, its highest weekly share in two years and the second highest ever.

crypto.summary: Base expanded its tokenized stock roster with $AAPLc and additional tickers now tradeable and composable as DeFi primitives.

crypto.summary: Zones proving is coming soon to Tempo, the stablecoin settlement layer currently running in no-proof mode that underpins Stripe's Link balance for agentic payments.

fintech.summary: Many fintechs stitch together vendors across payments, fraud, and money movement. The result: a fragmented stack that slows you down. fintech.title: S&P Dow Jones partners with Kalshi for index-based events contracts, use prediction data
fintech.summary: Kalshi will offer event contracts settled against official S&P Dow Jones index values, while S&P plans to turn Kalshi's probability data into new benchmarks covering economics, politics, and sports. The agreement gives the prediction-market operator institutional credibility amid ongoing gambling-related criticism and moves event contracts closer to mainstream financial-market infrastructure.

fintech.title: Ripple gets OCC's unconditional charter approval
fintech.summary: Ripple has secured final OCC approval to launch a national trust bank, allowing it to provide digital asset custody and manage reserves backing its RLUSD stablecoin, but not accept deposits or make commercial loans. The company is also expanding its BNY partnership to support institutional custody and tokenized assets, explore tokenized trade finance, and eventually let clients mint and redeem RLUSD directly through the bank.

fintech.title: Personal AI assistant Instinct just gave AI agents their own spending money
fintech.summary: Instinct lets users fund a wallet and set spending limits so AI agents can make purchases independently. Stablecoins are converted into dollars and spent through a Visa virtual card, letting merchants accept payment through existing infrastructure. The broader tension is over who controls agent payments: Stripe's virtual cards or Visa and Mastercard's competing systems tied to customers' existing cards.

fintech.title: Meet the ghost card
fintech.summary: Fintech is rapidly converging around agents, stablecoins, and programmable money: Meta's Muse is driving real consumer agentic commerce, Ramp is pushing deeper into treasury and digital-asset infrastructure, Mercury has crossed $1 billion of annualized revenue, and Visa plus Mesh are turning wallet balances into card-network spending through invisible “ghost cards.” The financial stack is shifting from apps and standalone products toward agent-controlled money movement, embedded credit, tokenized assets, and new trust layers around identity, permissions, and liability.

fintech.title: Anthropic IPO: S-1 breakdown
fintech.summary: Anthropic's S-1 shows extraordinary growth and operating leverage: $16.3 billion of first-half 2026 revenue, roughly 900% net revenue retention, more than $6.6 million of trailing revenue per employee, and a profitable Q2, with consumption-based “pay-for-intelligence” generating 80% of revenue. The biggest questions are durability and infrastructure economics, as Anthropic remains highly dependent on cloud partners, faces enormous forward compute commitments, and operates in a market with low switching costs, even as customer usage and compute efficiency are improving at exceptional rates.

fintech.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach fintech builders and finance leaders where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities .

fintech.title: Ripple strikes deal with Robinhood to expand RLUSD stablecoin usage
fintech.summary: Ripple and Robinhood are expanding RLUSD across institutional trading, treasury management, and financing, with the stablecoin set to support settlement through Ripple Prime and Bitstamp while also being listed on Robinhood. The partnership shows stablecoins moving beyond crypto trading into 24/7 financial infrastructure, where issuers increasingly compete by bundling settlement, treasury, payments, and financing around their digital dollars.

fintech.title: Ramp launches Inspect, a collaborative coding agent for faster product development
fintech.summary: Ramp is opening early access to Inspect, a cloud-based coding agent that turns requests from Slack, GitHub, Linear, or the web into visually validated, reviewed pull requests inside a company's development environment. Ramp says Inspect now accounts for 74% of merged PRs and has helped builders ship 3.4x more PRs per person than a year ago, as the bottleneck shifts from writing code toward deciding which ideas are worth shipping.

fintech.title: RedotPay reportedly plans US IPO by year-end at up to $5B valuation
fintech.summary: Hong Kong-based stablecoin payments company RedotPay is reportedly preparing a confidential US IPO filing that could value the business at about $5 billion, with JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs advising. The company says it serves more than 9 million customers and has surpassed $180 million in annualized revenue, although the offering would come while RedotPay remains in an ongoing $473 million legal dispute with Binance.

fintech.title: Guidewire agrees to acquire hyperexponential for up to $2.1B
fintech.summary: Guidewire agreed to acquire AI-native underwriting platform hyperexponential for $1.7 billion in cash plus up to $400 million of contingent consideration, bringing hx's pricing and risk-decision technology into Guidewire's P&C insurance platform. The deal is aimed at accelerating “agentic underwriting,” where AI agents work alongside underwriters and actuaries across submission triage, pricing, and portfolio decisions, and Guidewire says hx already supports decisions across more than $75 billion of annual commercial P&C premium.

fintech.title: Fintech funding hits 2-year low in Q3
fintech.summary: Global fintech funding fell 29% year over year to $11 billion in Q3, its lowest level since Q3 2024, with just 650 deals recorded.

fintech.title: Hyphenate raises new funding to expand self-learning finance agents
fintech.summary: Hyphenate raised a new round led by Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from B Capital and existing investors, bringing total funding to $54 million.

it.summary: Unlimited AI budgets were nice while they lasted - but today's CIOs must justify every extra $ of AI spend. Understanding true cost of scaling AI means going beyond tokens, models, and infrastructure. Learn how to have that conversation by watching the recorded webinar with Gartner Director Analyst Akanksha Pandey , covering: How CIOs and CFOs can create cost transparency and shared accountability for AI spending Approaches for building investment discipline, outcome metrics and value-based governance How modernization can fund future growth by reducing structural costs and increasing reinvestment capacity The hidden cost drivers that emerge as AI initiatives scale Find more resources on the Gartner AI Hub

it.title: Google and Oracle are partnering to bring Google TPUs to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
it.summary: Google Cloud and Oracle are partnering to bring Google Tensor Processing Units to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, making OCI the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer TPUs. The companies plan to deploy TPU capacity on OCI starting in 2027 to help organizations scale AI workloads across data centers engineered for AI density.

it.title: OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips, The Information reports
it.summary: OpenAI reportedly plans to purchase Google's Tensor Processing Units, expanding beyond its existing chip-rental arrangement. The potential deal would give OpenAI another source of AI computing capacity alongside Nvidia GPUs and its custom-chip development efforts with Broadcom, while strengthening Google's position in the AI infrastructure market.

it.title: Microsoft beats quarterly cloud revenue estimates
it.summary: Microsoft's Azure cloud business reported $33.17 billion in quarterly revenue, growing 48% year over year and beating analyst expectations. Microsoft is now disclosing Azure revenue in dollars, providing greater visibility into its cloud performance as the company continues investing heavily in AI infrastructure.

it.title: Information overload is harming enterprise productivity - here's how IT leaders can solve that
it.summary: A Forrester study commissioned by Staffbase found that fragmented workplace communication is affecting employee productivity, with 48% of respondents reporting reduced efficiency and 44% citing more errors or missed deadlines. The findings suggest that consolidating information and connecting workplace applications could reduce unnecessary context switching.

it.title: What enterprises can learn from Anthropic's IPO prospectus about vendor dependency
it.summary: Anthropic's IPO prospectus reveals that nearly half of its sales are routed through cloud partners Amazon and Google, highlighting significant vendor dependency and concentration risk across the AI ecosystem. Industry experts advise enterprise CIOs to treat AI procurement as a resilience conversation by questioning supplier supply chains and ensuring data and workflow portability.

it.title: AI agents are now network identities: what IDC's new 2026 data says about access control [Read the Report]
it.summary: Shadow AI is the new Shadow IT. Unmanaged AI agents create unmonitored access risks across hybrid environments. IDC research reveals that detection alone isn't enough : closing the gap between risk detection and policy enforcement is the new benchmark. Learn how Portnox Cloud automates zero-trust access enforcement .

it.title: NVIDIA and Oracle Expand NVIDIA Vera Rubin to Multi-Gigawatt Scale
it.summary: NVIDIA and Oracle have announced plans to expand Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Superclusters with NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems to multi-gigawatt scale. The companies are also bringing NVIDIA Vera CPUs and Vera Rubin GPUs to OCI to support AI training, inference, and agentic workloads. OpenAI has also trained and served frontier models on OCI infrastructure powered by NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.

it.title: GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack
it.summary: GitHub has introduced a new Copilot app, Copilot Fusion, for automatically routing coding tasks across multiple AI models and agent workflows spanning repositories and development tools. GitHub also announced that Enterprise customers can access Copilot features without purchasing a separate subscription, with usage billed through AI credits.

it.title: Snowflake and Oracle: Bringing the AI Data Cloud to OCI
it.summary: Snowflake and Oracle are expanding their partnership to bring Snowflake's AI Data Cloud natively to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure as a first-party offering. Planned as an integrated service purchased and billed directly through Oracle, Snowflake on OCI aims to connect enterprise data across Oracle applications and databases with other sources to support analytics and AI workflows.

it.title: Discovering and exploiting vulnerabilities in critical, real-world software with Claude
it.summary: Anthropic researchers used an internal research model to discover critical vulnerabilities and construct sophisticated multi-step exploit chains in widely used software, including browsers, mobile operating systems, and kernel networking stacks. The model identified issues such as remote code execution, sandbox escapes, and lock-screen bypasses, which were reported to affected vendors under coordinated vulnerability disclosure. Anthropic argues that AI-assisted vulnerability discovery could help defenders identify and patch security flaws before attackers exploit them.

it.title: Oracle Cloud Acceleron adds AI-assisting networking enhancements
it.summary: Oracle expanded its Acceleron networking platform with new capabilities for AI and high-performance computing workloads. Updates include RDMA connectivity for front-end compute, expanded NVMe block-storage options, and communication libraries designed to maintain distributed AI workloads when network paths fail.

it.title: Microsoft urges Entra ID admins to migrate users to passkeys
it.summary: Microsoft is reminding Entra ID administrators to prepare for the February 2027 retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication.

it.title: Tesco eyes open source VMware alternative amid long-running spat
it.summary: A Tesco engineering job posting outlines plans to migrate the retailer's edge virtualization infrastructure from VMware to Proxmox, offering another example of an enterprise evaluating alternatives amid Broadcom's licensing changes.

it.title: Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 is now available on Google Cloud
it.summary: The specialized AI model serves as a high-level brain for robots across various physical embodiments, combining spatio-temporal video understanding, long-horizon planning, and agentic tool orchestration for enterprise production environments.
